title: Ship Ahoy

commands.name: SetCutoff
commands.doc: Glides the frequency of the filter to a note. The glide starts at the sample of the event whose hook calls it (plus the delay, and the lead of the clock for clock events) from where the frequency is; a command during a glide continues from the present value. The plugin has no other way to move the frequency: no script, no movement.

args.name: note
args.doc: MIDI note as a number, 69 = A4 = 440 Hz, fractions are cents; the frequency of the resonance peak, limited to 10 Hz up to a sixth of the sample rate

fields.name: ticks
fields.doc: length of the step in clock ticks (added to ms); with ms also 0 the step is the present step length of the Step setting

fields.name: ms
fields.doc: length of the step in milliseconds

fields.name: glide
fields.doc: the glide lasts this fraction of the step: 0 jumps at once, 0.5 glides during the first half and then holds, 1 arrives as the step ends

fields.name: delayTicks
fields.doc: start this many clock ticks after the event (added to delayMs)

fields.name: delayMs
fields.doc: start this many milliseconds after the event whose hook calls it

commands.name: SpeedRatio
commands.doc: Multiplies the speed of the clock (tempo, steps, ticks, timers set from now on), 0.1 to 10. It starts at the sample of the event plus the delay and, for clock events, the lead; a new script starts at 1.

args.name: ratio
args.doc: factor on the speed of the clock: 2 doubles the tempo, 0.5 halves it; 1 again at every new script

fields.name: delayTicks
fields.doc: start this many clock ticks after the event (added to delayMs)

fields.name: delayMs
fields.doc: start this many milliseconds after the event whose hook calls it

commands.name: SetResonance
commands.doc: Sets the resonance, smoothed over 20 ms. It stays until the next call; a script that does not call it gets 85. Applied at the sample of the event plus the lead (at once for an external event).

args.name: percent
args.doc: resonance as a fraction of self-oscillation at the present frequency: 100 is the edge, the top 10 ring hard and raise the level

commands.name: SetFilterType
commands.doc: Sets the type of the filter (low, band and high pass, notch, phasers; the FilterType constants). It stays until the next call; a script that does not call it gets Lp12.

args.name: type
args.doc: the pole-mixing preset of the filter

commands.name: SetDrift
commands.doc: Sets the drift: a slow random wobble added to the frequency, independent of the notes. It stays until the next call; a script that does not call it gets none.

args.name: depth
args.doc: standard deviation of the drift in semitones, 0 switches it off; peaks reach about three times as much

fields.name: rate
fields.doc: corner frequency of the drift in Hz

commands.name: SetTimer
commands.doc: Starts (or restarts) a timer; its hook OnTimer(id) is called when it is due. The delay is the length of ms and ticks together and is fixed when the timer is set. It counts from the event whose hook sets it.

fields.name: ticks
fields.doc: delay in clock ticks, added to ms (the length of a tick at the present tempo)

fields.name: repeating
fields.doc: fire again and again after the same delay

commands.name: GetX
commands.doc: The X knob of the plugin, whose meaning the script decides. Returns a number from 0 to 100.

commands.name: GetY
commands.doc: The Y knob of the plugin, whose meaning the script decides. Returns a number from 0 to 100.

hooks.name: OnStart
hooks.doc: Runs once after the script is loaded.

hooks.name: OnStep
hooks.doc: A step of the clock, as long as the Step setting says (1/16 by default), at the tempo and speed ratio of the moment; step counts from 0 at the start of the clock.

hooks.name: OnNewPitch
hooks.doc: A note was played into the plugin (one voice, 80 Hz to 1 kHz): about 80 ms after its start, once its pitch has been steady for three readings, and again when the same note is struck anew. note is the nearest MIDI note (69 = A4), hz its frequency, pitch the MIDI note with fractions (cents), periodicity how clearly periodic the sound was, 0 to 1 (1 minus the YIN difference at the period; not a probability), level the RMS of the last 25 ms, linear. The commands it calls are applied at the first block boundary after the note was reported, without the lead of the clock. Called only while the script defines it.

hooks.name: OnPitchEnd
hooks.doc: The note that was playing has ended (silence or noise for three readings, 60 ms); note is the note that ended. Its commands are applied at the first block boundary, like those of OnNewPitch.

hooks.name: OnControl
hooks.doc: X or Y was moved (0 to 100 each, both given), at most once per audio block and only on a change. Its commands are applied at the first block boundary, like those of OnNewPitch. GetX() and GetY() give the same values anywhere else. Called only while the script defines it.

hooks.name: OnTick
hooks.doc: A tick of the tempo clock (while the transport runs); tick counts from 0 at the start.

hooks.name: OnTransportStart
hooks.doc: The transport started; the clock begins with tick 0.

hooks.name: OnTimer
hooks.doc: A timer set with SetTimer is due.

enums.name: Ticks
enums.doc: Lengths of notes in ticks of the clock (96 per quarter note).

enums.name: FilterType
enums.doc: Types of the filter, for SetFilterType (the pole-mixing presets of the plugin).

libraries.summary: the last notes that were played into the plugin, for scripts that build their sequences from them.

members.name: remember
members.doc: an accepted note (OnNewPitch); the same note again is remembered again (a new attack)

members.name: played
members.doc: how many played notes are remembered, 0 to Notes.size

members.name: last
members.doc: the i-th newest played note (1 = newest), nil if there is none

members.name: window
members.doc: the notes to build from, oldest first: always Notes.size of them, the played ones preceded by the end of Notes.fallback while fewer than Notes.size were played, so a script sounds from the first step on and turns into the played notes one by one

members.name: pitchClasses
members.doc: the pitch classes (0 = C ... 11 = B) of the window, each once, ascending

members.name: has
members.doc: true if the window has a note of this pitch class

members.name: intervals
members.doc: the distances in semitones above `root` (0 to 11) of the pitch classes of the window, each once, ascending: 0 is the root itself

members.name: sequence
members.doc: a list of `length` notes: the window, repeated

examples.title: The smallest script
examples.summary: One note per step: OnStep and SetCutoff. Change the note (0 to 127, 69 = A4 = 440 Hz) and hear the filter ring at that pitch. Without a script the plugin has no way to move the frequency, so a call to SetCutoff is the minimum.
examples.code:
-- The smallest script
-- One note per step: OnStep and SetCutoff. Change the note (0 to 127, 69 = A4 = 440 Hz) and hear the filter ring at
-- that pitch. Without a script the plugin has no way to move the frequency, so a call to SetCutoff is the minimum.
function OnStep(step)
    SetCutoff(57)
end

examples.title: A list of notes with a glide
examples.summary: One note per step, taken in turn from a table. Shows step counting from 0 and the glide field (0 jumps, 1 arrives as the step ends). Change the notes, or the glide to 0.5 to arrive half way through each step and then hold.
examples.code:
-- A list of notes with a glide
-- One note per step, taken in turn from a table. Shows step counting from 0 and the glide field (0 jumps, 1 arrives
-- as the step ends). Change the notes, or the glide to 0.5 to arrive half way through each step and then hold.
local notes = { 57, 60, 64, 67, 64, 60 }

function OnStart()
    SetFilterType(FilterType.Lp12)
    SetResonance(80)
end

function OnStep(step)
    -- step starts at 0, Lua lists at 1
    SetCutoff(notes[step % #notes + 1], { glide = 0.7 })
end

examples.title: Random hold
examples.summary: A random note of a scale on every step. Shows math.random and picking from a list, and X and Y as knobs: X is the glide in percent of the step, Y the resonance. Change the scale and the root.
examples.code:
-- Random hold
-- A random note of a scale on every step. Shows math.random and picking from a list, and X and Y as knobs: X is the
-- glide in percent of the step, Y the resonance. Change the scale and the root.
local scale = { 0, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10 } -- natural minor, in semitones above the root
local root = 45                         -- A2

function OnStart()
    SetFilterType(FilterType.Lp24)
end

function OnControl(x, y)
    SetResonance(y)
end

function OnStep(step)
    local degree = math.random(#scale)
    local octave = math.random(0, 2)
    SetCutoff(root + scale[degree] + 12 * octave, { glide = math.max(0.01, GetX() / 100) })
end

examples.title: Speed changes on a timer
examples.summary: The sequence runs at normal speed for four seconds, then at double speed for two seconds, and so on. Shows SetTimer, OnTimer and SpeedRatio. A timer set while the speed is 2 follows that speed (see SpeedRatio in API.md).
examples.code:
-- Speed changes on a timer
-- The sequence runs at normal speed for four seconds, then at double speed for two seconds, and so on. Shows SetTimer,
-- OnTimer and SpeedRatio. A timer set while the speed is 2 follows that speed (see SpeedRatio in API.md).
local notes = { 52, 55, 59, 62 }
local fast = false

function OnStart()
    SetResonance(75)
    SetTimer(0, { ms = 4000 })
end

function OnTimer(id)
    fast = not fast
    SpeedRatio(fast and 2 or 1)
    SetTimer(0, { ms = 4000 })
end

function OnStep(step)
    SetCutoff(notes[step % #notes + 1], { glide = 0.5 })
end

examples.title: Follow what is played
examples.summary: The filter steps through the notes played into the plugin. Shows OnNewPitch and the factory library "notes". Until five notes were played the library's fallback scale is used, and the played notes push it out one by one. Play a few notes into the input and listen.
examples.code:
-- Follow what is played
-- The filter steps through the notes played into the plugin. Shows OnNewPitch and the factory library "notes". Until
-- five notes were played the library's fallback scale is used, and the played notes push it out one by one. Play a
-- few notes into the input and listen.
import "notes"

function OnNewPitch(note, hz, pitch, periodicity, level)
    Notes.remember(note)
end

function OnStep(step)
    local window = Notes.window()
    SetCutoff(window[step % #window + 1], { glide = 0.6 })
end

examples.title: Reset on transport start
examples.summary: Every start of the host's transport begins the pattern again at its first note, at normal speed, with a slow drift that stops with the transport. Shows OnTransportStart and OnTransportStop. The script keeps its own position in the pattern, so it can restart it whenever it likes.
examples.code:
-- Reset on transport start
-- Every start of the host's transport begins the pattern again at its first note, at normal speed, with a slow drift
-- that stops with the transport. Shows OnTransportStart and OnTransportStop. The script keeps its own position in the
-- pattern, so it can restart it whenever it likes.
local notes = { 60, 64, 67, 72 }
local index = 0

function OnTransportStart()
    index = 0
    SpeedRatio(1)
    SetDrift(0.5)
end

function OnTransportStop()
    SetDrift(0)
end

function OnStep(step)
    SetCutoff(notes[index % #notes + 1], { glide = 0.4 })
    index = index + 1
end

scripts.title: A trill: the steps alternate between the lower and the upper part of two octaves around middle C
scripts.summary: (each a little more than a third of the range), a glide to a random note inside the part. X: glide in percent of the step, 1 to 100 Y: resonance in percent, 0 to 100
scripts.code:
-- A trill: the steps alternate between the lower and the upper part of two octaves around middle C
-- (each a little more than a third of the range), a glide to a random note inside the part.
-- X: glide in percent of the step, 1 to 100
-- Y: resonance in percent, 0 to 100
local low = 48
local high = 72
local part = 0.4 * (high - low)

function OnStart()
    SetFilterType(FilterType.Lp12)
    SetResonance(GetY())
end

function OnControl(x, y)
    SetResonance(y)
end

function OnStep(step)
    local note
    if step % 2 == 0 then
        note = low + math.random() * part
    else
        note = high - math.random() * part
    end
    SetCutoff(note, { glide = math.max(0.01, GetX() / 100) })
end

scripts.title: Answers what is played: the newest note starts a phrase one octave above it that climbs through the pitch classes
scripts.summary: of the last five notes (see notes.lua) and comes back down, one per step. A new note starts the phrase again from its own pitch at the next step. X: glide in percent of the step, 1 to 100 (50 = half the step) Y: resonance in percent, 0 to 100
scripts.code:
-- Answers what is played: the newest note starts a phrase one octave above it that climbs through the pitch classes
-- of the last five notes (see notes.lua) and comes back down, one per step. A new note
-- starts the phrase again from its own pitch at the next step.
-- X: glide in percent of the step, 1 to 100 (50 = half the step)
-- Y: resonance in percent, 0 to 100
import "notes"

function OnStart()
    SetFilterType(FilterType.Lp12)
    SetResonance(GetY())
end

function OnControl(x, y)
    SetResonance(y)
end

local position = 0

function OnNewPitch(note, hz, pitch, periodicity, level)
    Notes.remember(note)
    position = 0
end

function OnStep(step)
    local root = Notes.last(1) or Notes.fallback[1]
    local distances = Notes.intervals(root)
    local count = #distances
    local period = math.max(1, 2 * count - 2)
    local k = position % period
    local index = k < count and k + 1 or period - k + 1
    SetCutoff(root + 12 + distances[index], { glide = math.max(0.01, GetX() / 100) })
    position = position + 1
end

scripts.title: Echoes what is played: at the first step after a note arrived the filter glides to that very note and stays there until the next note. It starts on the first note of the fallback in notes.lua
scripts.summary: X: glide in percent of the step, 1 to 100 (20 = a fifth of the step) Y: resonance in percent, 0 to 100
scripts.code:
-- Echoes what is played: at the first step after a note arrived the filter glides to that very note and stays there until the next note. It starts on the first note of the fallback in notes.lua.
-- X: glide in percent of the step, 1 to 100 (20 = a fifth of the step)
-- Y: resonance in percent, 0 to 100
import "notes"

function OnStart()
    SetFilterType(FilterType.Lp12)
    SetResonance(GetY())
end

function OnControl(x, y)
    SetResonance(y)
end

local target = Notes.fallback[1]
local fresh = true

function OnNewPitch(note, hz, pitch, periodicity, level)
    Notes.remember(note)
    target = pitch
    fresh = true
end

function OnStep(step)
    if fresh then
        SetCutoff(target, { glide = math.max(0.01, GetX() / 100) })
        fresh = false
    end
end

scripts.title: Follows what is played: the filter steps through the last five notes played into the plugin, oldest to newest,
scripts.summary: one per step. Until five notes were played the sequence begins with the end of the fallback scale of notes.lua, and the played notes push it out one by one. X: glide in percent of the step, 1 to 100 (70 is a flowing line) Y: resonance in percent, 0 to 100
scripts.code:
-- Follows what is played: the filter steps through the last five notes played into the plugin, oldest to newest,
-- one per step. Until five notes were played the sequence begins with the end of the
-- fallback scale of notes.lua, and the played notes push it out one by one.
-- X: glide in percent of the step, 1 to 100 (70 is a flowing line)
-- Y: resonance in percent, 0 to 100
import "notes"

function OnStart()
    SetFilterType(FilterType.Lp12)
    SetResonance(GetY())
end

function OnControl(x, y)
    SetResonance(y)
end

function OnNewPitch(note, hz, pitch, periodicity, level)
    Notes.remember(note)
end

function OnStep(step)
    local window = Notes.window()
    SetCutoff(window[step % #window + 1], { glide = math.max(0.01, GetX() / 100) })
end

scripts.title: Hop: the classic Ship Ahoy. On every step the filter frequency jumps to a random note inside three octaves around
scripts.summary: 1 kHz and glides there; white random (every note of the range is equally likely). X: glide in percent of the step, 1 to 100 (5 = a short glide, 100 = glides all the way to the next step) Y: resonance in percent, 0 to 100 (85 = the classic, above 95 it rings hard)
scripts.code:
-- Hop: the classic Ship Ahoy. On every step the filter frequency jumps to a random note inside three octaves around
-- 1 kHz and glides there; white random (every note of the range is equally likely).
-- X: glide in percent of the step, 1 to 100 (5 = a short glide, 100 = glides all the way to the next step)
-- Y: resonance in percent, 0 to 100 (85 = the classic, above 95 it rings hard)
local centre = 69 + 12 * math.log(1000 / 440, 2) -- 1 kHz as a MIDI note
local range = 36                                 -- three octaves, in semitones

function OnStart()
    SetFilterType(FilterType.Lp12)
    SetResonance(GetY())
end

function OnControl(x, y)
    SetResonance(y)
end

function OnStep(step)
    SetCutoff(centre + (math.random() - 0.5) * range, { glide = math.max(0.01, GetX() / 100) })
end

scripts.title: Sample and hold: a random note inside two octaves around middle C on every step, a glide to it
scripts.summary: X: glide in percent of the step, 1 to 100 Y: resonance in percent, 0 to 100
scripts.code:

-- X: glide in percent of the step, 1 to 100
-- Y: resonance in percent, 0 to 100
function OnStart()

    SetResonance(GetY())
end

function OnControl(x, y)
    SetResonance(y)
end

function OnStep(step)

end

scripts.title: A fixed sequence of eight notes, one per step
scripts.summary: The step length is the Step setting, the speed the Tempo knob (or the host's tempo). X: glide in percent of the step, 1 to 100 (70 reaches each note shortly before the next step) Y: resonance in percent, 0 to 100
scripts.code:
-- A fixed sequence of eight notes, one per step.
-- The step length is the Step setting, the speed the Tempo knob (or the host's tempo).
-- X: glide in percent of the step, 1 to 100 (70 reaches each note shortly before the next step)
-- Y: resonance in percent, 0 to 100
local notes = { 57, 60, 64, 67, 64, 60, 62, 59 }

function OnStart()
    SetFilterType(FilterType.Lp12)
    SetResonance(GetY())
end

function OnControl(x, y)
    SetResonance(y)
end

function OnStep(step)
    SetCutoff(notes[step % #notes + 1], { glide = math.max(0.01, GetX() / 100) })

scripts.title: Slow drift: a slow wander. On every step the filter frequency moves to a note a little away from the last one
scripts.summary: (a random walk around 800 Hz, four octaves wide, remembering about ten steps), gliding all the way, with a 24 dB lowpass and a gentle wobble on top. Meant for a slow tempo (30 BPM at 1/16). X: drift depth in percent, 0 to 100 (50 = 1.5 semitones of wobble, 100 = 3) Y: resonance in percent, 0 to 100
scripts.code:
-- Slow drift: a slow wander. On every step the filter frequency moves to a note a little away from the last one
-- (a random walk around 800 Hz, four octaves wide, remembering about ten steps), gliding all the way, with a
-- 24 dB lowpass and a gentle wobble on top. Meant for a slow tempo (30 BPM at 1/16).
-- X: drift depth in percent, 0 to 100 (50 = 1.5 semitones of wobble, 100 = 3)
-- Y: resonance in percent, 0 to 100
local centre = 69 + 12 * math.log(800 / 440, 2) -- 800 Hz as a MIDI note
local range = 48                                -- four octaves, in semitones
local memory = 0.905                            -- correlation of consecutive steps
local deviation = 0.2                           -- standard deviation of the walk, as a fraction of the range
local state = 0

local function gauss()
    return math.sqrt(-2 * math.log(1 - math.random())) * math.cos(2 * math.pi * math.random())
end

local function wobble(x)
    SetDrift(x * 0.03, { rate = 0.5 })
end

function OnStart()
    SetFilterType(FilterType.Lp24)
    SetResonance(GetY())
    wobble(GetX())
end

function OnControl(x, y)
    SetResonance(y)
    wobble(x)
end

function OnStep(step)
    state = memory * state + math.sqrt(1 - memory * memory) * gauss()
    local position = clamp(0.5 + deviation * state, 0, 1)
    SetCutoff(centre + (position - 0.5) * range, { glide = 1 })
end

scripts.title: Toggle trill: a trill between low and high. The steps alternate between the lower and the upper 40 % of three
scripts.summary: octaves around 1 kHz, a random note inside the part each time, with a band pass (6 dB). X: glide in percent of the step, 1 to 100 Y: resonance in percent, 0 to 100
scripts.code:
-- Toggle trill: a trill between low and high. The steps alternate between the lower and the upper 40 % of three
-- octaves around 1 kHz, a random note inside the part each time, with a band pass (6 dB).
-- X: glide in percent of the step, 1 to 100
-- Y: resonance in percent, 0 to 100
local centre = 69 + 12 * math.log(1000 / 440, 2) -- 1 kHz as a MIDI note
local range = 36                                 -- three octaves, in semitones
local spread = 0.4                               -- the part of the range a step may land in
local high = false

function OnStart()
    SetFilterType(FilterType.Bp6)
    SetResonance(GetY())
end

function OnControl(x, y)
    SetResonance(y)
end

function OnStep(step)
    high = not high
    local offset = math.random() * spread
    local position = high and 1 - offset or offset
    SetCutoff(centre + (position - 0.5) * range, { glide = math.max(0.01, GetX() / 100) })
end

guide:
# Writing a Ship Ahoy script (guide for an AI assistant)

Ship Ahoy is a filter that rings like a resonator. It has no way to move on its own: a Lua script decides, step by
step, where the frequency goes. This file tells you how to work here. It holds no names, ranges or limits of the API:
those are in `API.md` and `constants.lua` next to it, generated from the plugin, and always right. Read them first.

## 1. What a script is, and what is in this folder

- A script is one Lua 5.4 text file. Its top-level code runs once when it is loaded. After that the plugin calls the
  hooks the script defines (global functions such as `OnStep`), and the script answers by calling commands (global
  functions such as `SetCutoff`). A hook that is not defined is not called.
- Commands do not return anything to hear; they tell the plugin what to do and when (the event's time plus an optional
  delay). The getters (`GetX`, `GetY`) read the two knobs of the plugin.
- Files here: `API.md` (every command, hook, constant, library and limit), `constants.lua` (the named constants, already
  global in every script), `examples/` (small scripts that run as they are), and the factory scripts (`hop.lua`,
  `sequence.lua`, ..., plus the library `notes.lua`). The factory scripts are read only.

## 2. Where a script goes

- On the Dwarf a script is a file `/data/jaypacks/scripts/shipahoy/user-1.lua` up to `user-8.lua`. Reach it with
  `ssh root@192.168.51.1` and `scp`; the data partition survives a plugin update.
- Select it with the plugin's Script setting (User 1 to User 8). The factory scripts cannot be edited: to change one, or
  an example, copy it to a user slot.
- A script may `import "notes"` (a factory library, see `API.md`); it cannot read other files, and `io`, `os`, `require`
  and `load` do not exist.

## 3. The loop to follow

1. Write the script to a user slot.
2. The plugin notices the saved file within a second and reloads it. Nothing is restarted.
3. Read `/data/jaypacks/scripts/shipahoy/user-1.log` (same name as the script, `.log`). It says whether the load worked,
   the message with the line of an error, the calls that were ignored, and every line the script wrote with `Log(...)`.
   The plugin's Script status output shows the same in a number (1 ok, 3 compile error, 4 runtime error, 5 over the
   budget, 6 out of memory).
4. Fix what the log says and save again.

A script that fails to load (syntax error, error at the top level or in `OnStart`) is rejected and the previous script
keeps sounding, so a typo never silences the plugin; but the new script is not running either. Always read the log after
a save. An error in a hook ends only that call; the next event runs again.

## 4. Rules in short

- Hooks are global functions with fixed names and argument lists (`API.md`, Hooks). Write `function OnStep(step)`, not
  a local.
- Commands take positional arguments and, last, an optional table of named fields:
  `SetCutoff(60, { glide = 0.5 })`. A field is written by name; there is no other order.
- Units: notes are MIDI notes (69 = 440 Hz, fractions are cents); the clock has 96 ticks per quarter note; time
  fields are in milliseconds (`ms`, `delayMs`) or ticks (`ticks`, `delayTicks`). `GetX()` and `GetY()` give 0 to 100.
- `step` and `tick` count from 0; a Lua list starts at 1: use `notes[step % #notes + 1]`.
- `import "name"` runs a library once, then its global table is there (`import "notes"` gives `Notes`).
- Randomness is `math.random`; it gives the same numbers on every run. Keep state in locals at the top of the script.
- Do work in the hook, not in loops that wait: a hook has a small budget of instructions and milliseconds.
- A number field outside its range is clamped. An integer argument (a timer id, a filter type) outside its range, or not
  whole, makes the call ignored and is written to the log. A field name the command does not know is ignored and
  logged. A wrong type or a missing argument is an error in the hook.

## 5. Mistakes seen most

Each line is a message the plugin writes to the log, and the fix.

| Log says | Cause and fix |
| --- | --- |
| `SetCutoff: unknown field 'glid' is ignored` | The field is misspelt; take the name from `API.md`. |
| `SetTimer: 'id' = 9 is outside 0..7, call ignored` | An integer argument out of range; the call did nothing. |
| `SetTimer: 'id' = 1.5 is not a whole number, call ignored` | An integer argument must be whole: use `math.floor`. |
| `SetCutoff expects 1 argument(s) and got 0` | A command called without its arguments. |
| `SetCutoff: the last argument must be a table of fields, not number` | Named fields go in braces: `{ glide = 0.5 }`. |
| `SetCutoff: 'note' must be a number, not nil` | A variable that is nil, often a list index one past the end (lists start at 1). |
| attempt to call a nil value (global 'SetCutof') | A misspelt command or hook name. Names are case sensitive. |
| the script sounds like the previous one | It was rejected at load; the log has the reason. |
| nothing moves | No hook that calls `SetCutoff` is defined, or the hook name is misspelt (`OnStep`, not `onStep`). |

Also: `glide` is a fraction of the step (0 to 1), while `GetX()` is a percent (0 to 100): divide by 100.
